President Donald Trump’s job approval rating in Alabama remains above water, though it has declined from the high point he reached at the start of his second term, according to the latest tracking data from Civiqs.

The survey shows 53% of Alabama voters approve of Trump’s job performance, while 40% disapprove. Another 8% said they neither approve nor disapprove. [...] The latest figures mark a modest improvement from early July, when 52% of Alabama voters approved of Trump’s job performance, 41% disapproved and 7% were unsure or held no opinion.

However, Trump’s standing remains below where it was at the beginning of his second term.

President Donald Trump’s job approval rating – 34% as of mid-July – has changed little over the last few months. But it is lower than his rating at a comparable point in his first term – 40% in August 2018 – and those of most other recent presidents at similar stages in their tenures.

July 23Trump’s 34% approval rating is unchanged from April, with 64% saying they disapprove of his job performance, according to a Pew Research Center survey of 3,554 U.S. adults conducted July 6-12 (margin of error 1.9).

The survey found Democrats have a six-point edge on the congressional midterm ballot, with 20% undecided. [...] However, Republicans still approve of Trump’s job as president, according to the poll, with 76% approving his job performance, down slightly from 85% recorded by the pollster in June.

The poll of 963 registered voters was taken July 23-27 and has a margin of error of 4.1.
